facts.title: Sergei Parajanov
facts.text: “Everyone knows that I have three motherlands”: Georgia, Ukraine and Armenia, he said in 1988.

facts.title: Shadows of Forgotten Ancestors
facts.text: Filmed in the Carpathians in the Hutsul dialect, it won awards at the Rome and Mar del Plata festivals.

facts.title: The Color of Pomegranates
facts.text: The life of Sayat-Nova told in tableaux vivants. The authorities imposed cuts and a re-edit.

facts.title: Five years of hard labor
facts.text: Arrested in December 1973, he was sentenced to a strict-regime camp after a fabricated trial.

facts.title: Creating without a camera
facts.text: Hundreds of drawings, small dolls, collages, and medallions etched with a nail onto kefir bottle caps.

facts.title: Released early
facts.text: Fellini, Tarkovsky, Godard and Truffaut rallied; Louis Aragon personally intervened with Brezhnev.

facts.title: The Parajanov Museum
facts.text: He died in Yerevan on July 20, 1990, and rests in the Pantheon. The museum houses his drawings and collages.

ytTitle: Sergei Parajanov, the filmmaker who never stopped creating
ytLead: Born in Tbilisi in 1924 into an Armenian family, Sergei Parajanov made Shadows of Forgotten Ancestors and The Color of Pomegranates, and kept creating even in a Soviet prison camp.
